title: Habits and a temporary change
prompt: Describe the normal routine of an invented student and a temporary change this week. Include two habits, two actions happening now and one state such as ownership or a preference.
checks: My habitual actions use the present simple.
My temporary actions use be + verb-ing.
My subject and verb agree.
I checked whether a state verb needs a simple form.

title: A past routine and an interruption
prompt: Tell a short fictional story about an old place. Describe what it used to be like, a repeated action and an activity that was interrupted by one event.
checks: I distinguished former states from repeated actions.
I used the past continuous for background.
My completed events use past simple forms.
I used did with a base verb in questions or negatives.

title: A progress letter
prompt: Write to an invented tutor about a project. Explain what you have completed, what you have been working on and what you have not done yet. Ask for a meeting. Invent any names or details.
checks: I connected recent work with the present.
I used past simple for a finished time.
I distinguished completed results from ongoing work.
My request and the reason for writing are clear.

title: Before the event
prompt: Describe an invented event and the preparation that happened before it. Include an earlier completed action, an earlier activity with a duration, and three later events in order.
checks: I used past perfect to look further back.
I used had been + verb-ing for duration.
I kept the main story in the past.
The reader can understand the order of events.

title: Plans for a move
prompt: Write a fictional message about a club or workplace move. Include an arrangement, an intention, an offer and one prediction. Use whichever future form fits your meaning.
checks: My arrangement has a clear future time.
I used going to with the base verb.
My offer or promise uses will accurately.
I marked predictions as predictions rather than established facts.

title: An organised future
prompt: Describe the timetable for an invented group project. Say what will be happening at a future time, what will have been completed by a deadline and how long preparation will have continued. Include a future time clause.
checks: I distinguished activity from completed results.
I used have + past participle in the future perfect.
My time clause uses an appropriate present form.
I made the reference times and durations clear.

title: A room description and spoken rehearsal
prompt: Describe an imagined room, the furniture already there and what a group still needs. Write a short plan, then practise saying it aloud. Use countable and uncountable nouns and different quantity expressions.
checks: I checked noun countability in the intended meaning.
I used is or are appropriately.
I distinguished few from a few and little from a little.
I practised explaining the room aloud; this is self-review.

title: Introducing a collection
prompt: Introduce an invented display or collection. Mention an item for the first time and then refer to it again. Use each or every, both or neither, and a clear possessive phrase.
checks: I chose a or an by the following sound.
I used the when the item was identifiable.
My group words have the correct noun and verb forms.
I avoided putting an article before my, this or another determiner.

title: A clear chain of reference
prompt: Describe two fictional people completing a task together. Use pronouns to avoid unnecessary repetition, but make every reference clear. Include a reflexive and a mutual action.
checks: My subject and object pronouns have the right forms.
Each pronoun clearly refers to the intended person or item.
I distinguished themselves from each other.
I used it and there for their different purposes.

title: Describing an experience precisely
prompt: Describe an invented exhibition or event. Use adjectives to describe objects and adverbs to explain actions. Include one pair such as interesting/interested and a carefully placed frequency adverb.
checks: My adjectives describe nouns or follow linking verbs.
My adverbs describe the intended actions or qualities.
I distinguished hard from hardly.
I distinguished the cause of a feeling from the person feeling it.

title: A comparison report
prompt: Use the fictional workshop figures in this unit: design 20 then 30; writing 40 then 40. Write a short overview and compare the two rounds. Describe only the given data; do not invent causes.
checks: I included an overview.
I used accurate comparatives and quantity words.
I checked the numbers and the comparison base.
I distinguished the data from explanations the data do not provide.

title: Compact descriptions
prompt: Describe an invented display using noun phrases. Include a prepositional phrase, an active -ing clause, a passive past-participle clause and a noun followed by a to-infinitive.
checks: Each noun phrase has a clear main noun.
My participle form matches an active or passive relationship.
My to-infinitive follows an appropriate noun.
My extra detail is clear without unnecessary words.

title: Cautious explanations
prompt: Describe a fictional situation with incomplete evidence. Give two possible explanations, one strong deduction with a clear basis, and one statement about ability. Make uncertainty explicit.
checks: I used a base verb after a modal.
My deductions and established facts are clearly different.
I used modal + have + participle for a past possibility.
I did not treat a possibility as proof.

title: Rules, options and advice
prompt: Write a notice for an invented workshop. Give two requirements, one prohibition, one optional action and one recommendation. Make their different strengths clear.
checks: I distinguished must not from do not have to.
My advice is not written as a compulsory rule.
I used correct forms for past or future requirements if included.
The fictional setting and intended reader are clear.

title: A meeting report
prompt: Invent a short club discussion and report it the next day. Include a statement, a yes/no question, an information question, a promise and a reminder. Make any changes of time or person explicit.
checks: My reporting verbs use the right patterns.
Reported questions have statement word order.
My pronouns and time references match the later viewpoint.
I chose backshift according to the stated context.

title: Learning through action
prompt: Describe an invented learning experience. Use decide to, enjoy doing, an object + infinitive pattern and a verb whose meaning changes with its following form. Explain the meaning you intend.
checks: My second verb follows the correct pattern.
I checked whether an object is needed.
I used to after made in a passive if included.
Remember, stop or another changing-meaning verb expresses my intended meaning.

title: Conditions for a plan
prompt: Invent a club plan. Describe a regular rule, an open future possibility and an unreal present situation. Add a precaution using in case and a condition using unless or provided that.
checks: The tense pattern matches the kind of condition.
Unless has the intended negative meaning.
In case introduces a precaution.
My imagined situation is distinguishable from a real plan.

title: Different past, different present
prompt: Tell a fictional story about a missed opportunity. Imagine a different past result, a present result of a past change, and one regret. Avoid using a real person’s private experiences.
checks: My third conditional uses had + participle and would have + participle.
The two times in my mixed conditional are clear.
My wish matches a present situation or a past regret.
I used should have to evaluate a past action if included.

title: A clear application
prompt: Write a fictional message applying to a club or course. Explain what you are interested in, what you are good at, your reason for applying and how the organiser can reply within the story. Use invented details without real contact information.
checks: I checked the whole adjective, verb or noun phrase.
Any verb after a preposition uses the correct form.
I used direct objects where a preposition is not needed.
My manner and time phrases have appropriate prepositions.

title: Identifying and adding detail
prompt: Describe an invented event using defining and non-defining relatives. Include whose, an object relative whose pronoun can be omitted, and one formal preposition + relative pronoun.
checks: My defining clauses identify the intended noun.
My extra information has appropriate commas.
I avoided repeating a subject or object inside the relative.
My relative pronouns and prepositions fit their functions.

title: A coherent proposal
prompt: Write a short fictional proposal for a learning club. Begin with the main issue, connect known ideas to new information and emphasise one priority with an it-cleft or what-clause. Use ellipsis only where the meaning stays clear.
checks: My subjects help the reader follow the topic.
My references connect to clear earlier ideas.
An omitted phrase remains easy to recover.
My emphasis highlights the intended point.

title: A process description
prompt: Describe the imaginary guide-printing sequence in this unit: check the text; print the pages; fold and cover them; count and store the guides. Use passive forms and sequence markers. Do not add unstated technical details.
checks: My passive uses be + past participle.
My tense stays consistent.
I named agents only where useful.
My stages follow the given process.

title: A linked explanation
prompt: Explain a fictional choice between two options. Use a reason, a result, a contrast, an additional point and a brief conclusion. Choose clause or noun-phrase structures that match each linker.
checks: Each link expresses the intended relationship.
I used a clause after because or although.
I used a noun phrase or ing form after because of or despite.
My punctuation separates linking adverbials clearly.

title: A position with limits
prompt: Write a short argument about an invented learning-club policy. State your view, attribute one fictional alternative view, give a reason and identify a limitation in the evidence. Do not present invented survey results as real research.
checks: My personal position is clear.
Other people’s claims are attributed.
My certainty matches the evidence in the fictional scenario.
My stance adverbs and evaluative adjectives are placed clearly.

title: Reporting change with noun phrases
prompt: Report these invented figures: club participation was 30 in Round 1 and 45 in Round 2. Describe the change with both a verb and a nominalisation, then write a short overview without inventing causes or satisfaction results.
checks: My noun forms are accurate.
Adjectives modify nouns and adverbs modify verbs.
I distinguished an increase of an amount from an increase in a variable.
My report includes only what the given figures support.
